name: Cambodia
description: Cambodia is a highly affordable Southeast Asian nation that appeals to expats seeking a low cost of living, flexible visa options, and a rich cultural experience. It offers a unique blend of ancient history and a developing economy, making it an attractive destination for retirees, entrepreneurs, and digital nomads alike.
longdescription: Expat life in Cambodia offers a fascinating blend of traditional Khmer culture and burgeoning modernity. Major cities like Phnom Penh and Siem Reap are hubs for expats, providing diverse job opportunities in education, NGOs, and growing business sectors. The cost of living is significantly lower than in many Western countries, allowing for a comfortable lifestyle on a modest budget. While the local language is Khmer, English is widely spoken, particularly in urban and tourist areas, easing communication for newcomers. The society is generally welcoming towards foreigners, often greeting them with a 'Khmer smile' and treating them as special guests. The economy is growing, with a dollarized system that provides stability for many Western expats. However, it is still a developing country, meaning infrastructure outside major cities can be patchy, and access to high-quality healthcare may require travel to neighboring countries. Expats often enjoy dining out due to its affordability and variety, and there's no shortage of activities, from exploring ancient temples to enjoying vibrant city nightlife. Challenges include navigating bureaucracy, occasional corruption, and concerns regarding safety, particularly street crime and road conditions.

visas.name: Cambodia E-Class Visa (Tourist)
visas.description: The E-class tourist visa allows entry for tourism and can be extended multiple times inside Cambodia, making it popular with long-stay visitors and expats.
benefits: Easy to obtain online or on arrival

visas.name: Cambodia Ordinary Resident Visa
visas.description: Long-term resident visa for retirees and self-sufficient individuals wanting to live in Cambodia. One of the most flexible and affordable expat visas in Southeast Asia.
required_documents: Bank statement or proof of funds

extra_info:
### Visas & Notes
- E-Class (tourist/business) visa: extendable up to 1 year
- Ordinary Resident visa available for retirees and investors
- No capital gains tax; USD widely accepted

Citizenship by Descent.desc: Citizenship is automatically granted to individuals born to at least one Cambodian parent, regardless of their place of birth.

Naturalization.desc: Foreigners can apply for naturalization after a continuous residence of at least seven years with a valid residence permit. This period can be reduced to three years for foreign spouses of Cambodian citizens. Applicants must demonstrate good conduct, a clean criminal record, proficiency in the Khmer language and script, an understanding of Cambodian history, and the ability to integrate harmoniously into Khmer society. Naturalization is not a right but a favor granted by the Kingdom of Cambodia, and applications can be rejected by discretion. Investment options are also available, typically through a significant donation of at least USD $250,000 to the national budget or a project investment of USD $312,500 or more, which may waive the residency requirement.

Birthright.desc: Cambodia has restricted *jus soli* provisions. Citizenship is granted to children born in Cambodia to a citizen parent. It is also granted to children born in Cambodia to foreign parents if both parents were themselves born and are living legally in Cambodia. Foundlings (children with unknown parents) discovered within Cambodia also automatically acquire Khmer citizenship.

Spouse and Family.desc: Foreign spouses of Cambodian nationals are eligible to apply for naturalization after three years of marriage, provided the marriage is properly registered. The usual residency requirement may be reduced to one year in specific cases.

tax_advice:
*   **Corporate Tax:** The standard corporate income tax (CIT) rate is 20%. Oil and gas, and certain mineral exploitation activities are subject to a 30% rate, while insurance companies are taxed at 5% on gross premiums. Qualified Investment Projects (QIPs) may receive tax holidays.
*   **Personal Income Tax (Tax on Salary - TOS):** For residents, the monthly cash salary is subject to progressive rates ranging from 0% to 20%. Non-residents are taxed at a flat rate of 20% on Cambodian-sourced salary. Fringe benefits are also taxed at a flat 20%. Resident individuals are taxed on worldwide income, while non-residents are taxed only on Cambodian-sourced income. Tax relief for residents includes allowances for dependent children and spouses.
*   **Value Added Tax (VAT):** The standard VAT rate in Cambodia is 10%, applicable to most goods and services. A 0% VAT rate applies to exported goods and services, as well as specific qualified supplies by Supporting Industry QIPs.
*   **Capital Gains Tax:** Cambodia enacted a capital gains tax in 2020, but its implementation on real estate for physical persons has been postponed until the end of 2025. When implemented, it will be 20% on the disposal of immovable property, shares, and other qualifying assets.
*   **Minimum Tax:** A minimum tax of 1% of annual turnover applies to self-declaration regime taxpayers, but it is not applicable to enterprises maintaining proper accounting records.
local_tips:
*   **Cost of Living:** Cambodia offers one of the lowest costs of living in Asia. A single expat can live comfortably on $800-$1,200 per month in cities like Phnom Penh, and even less in smaller towns like Siem Reap or Kampot. Rent for a one-bedroom apartment in a city center can range from $240 to $740.
*   **Language:** The official language is Khmer. While English is increasingly spoken in major cities and tourist areas, learning some basic Khmer phrases will be highly appreciated and beneficial for daily interactions.
*   **Safety:** Exercise a high degree of caution due to street crime (snatch-and-grab thefts by motorcyclists are common), road accidents (often involving drunk drivers and disregard for traffic laws), and scams. Avoid displaying valuables and be vigilant in crowded areas. Landmines and unexploded ordnance are still found in remote areas, particularly along the Thai border; do not touch unknown metal objects and use local guides in forested or dry rice paddy areas.
*   **Registration:** Since July 1, 2024, an online e-Arrival Card is mandatory for all travelers, to be completed within 7 days before arrival. All foreigners, whether residents or tourists, must also be registered in the Foreigners Present in Cambodia System (FPCS) by their accommodation provider or by self-registration if they own their accommodation. Failure to register with FPCS can lead to denial of visa extensions.
*   **Healthcare:** Medical facilities are limited, especially outside city centers. Many expats opt for private facilities or travel to neighboring countries like Thailand or Singapore for serious medical issues. Comprehensive health insurance is highly recommended.
*   **Visa:** Cambodia offers relatively easy and flexible visa options. Most visitors start with a tourist visa (T-class, 30 days, extendable once) or an Ordinary (E-class) visa (30 days, indefinitely renewable with subcategories for business/work (EB), retirement (ER), or student (ES)).
